main_contribution: We define plaque vulnerability indices (VI) as stress/strength ratios, show that pulsatile amplitude of plaque structural stress (ΔPSS) is the clinically appropriate stress metric, demonstrate the need to normalize by fibrous-cap strength, and quantify via surrogate-based Sobol analysis that material properties (especially E_vessel and E_fc) dominate VI variability.

nodes.text: Vulnerability index (VI) should be defined as stress/strength and stress is best interpreted as the pulsatile amplitude ΔPSS (fatigue perspective), implying the need for pulsatile FSI simulations.
ΔPSS (심주기 진폭, fatigue view) is a stronger/clinically more consistent predictor than peak PSS.
Capturing ΔPSS requires pulsatile (time-resolved) FSI; quasi-static or steady simulations cannot represent fatigue-related amplitudes.
Vulnerability indices must normalize stress by fibrous-cap strength (E_fc^α); strength-normalization choice materially affects VI behavior.
Including E_fc^α in the denominator yields VIs with greater agreement to established clinical high-risk plaque features than stress-only metrics.
The exponent α (e.g., 0.5 vs 1.0) modulates sensitivity of VI to material properties and thus influences sensitivity rankings.
Material properties dominate VI variability (Material > Hemodynamics > Morphology); key determinants are vessel wall stiffness, fibrous-cap stiffness, systolic blood pressure and pulse pressure.
Group-level Sobol indices show the material-property group has the largest first-order contribution (e.g., S1 ≈ 0.75 for LAP·VI2).
Individual-parameter Sobol results identify E_vessel and E_fc as the top contributors, followed by SBP and PP (e.g., E_fc S1 ≈ 0.55 for LAP·VI2).
Two selected VIs (VI1=ΔPSS/E_fc^0.5, VI2=ΔPSS/E_fc^1.0) satisfy all seven established clinical high-risk plaque criteria and show promising diagnostic separation (surrogate-evaluated).
VI1 and VI2 achieved mean sign-consistency scores of 1.00 against seven clinical high-risk criteria (95% BCa CI 0.99–1.00).
VI2 demonstrates diagnostic separation on a synthetic high-risk label (AUC ≈ 0.84; Youden sensitivity ≈0.78, specificity ≈0.76) when evaluated via the GPR surrogate.

Pulsatile partitioned strong-coupling FSI simulation of idealized coronary artery plaque models (LAP and CP) using BDF2 time integration, Δt=0.5 ms, 1600 steps/cardiac cycle, 3 cycles to periodic steady state; Neo-Hookean vessel/fibrous cap and linear-elastic core/calcification; boundary conditions from inflow/elastance time series; mesh/time independence verified
Mesh and time-step independence study: fluid mesh ~1.2M cells (min Δx=20 μm), solid mesh ~0.45M elements; coarse→fine and Δt/2 tests with peak PSS change <2%
Input design-space sampling and case generation: 1,000 LHS/other sampled parameter sets across morphology, hemodynamics, materials (columns per data/input_parameter/input.csv)
Postprocessing of FSI results to compute peak PSS, pulsatile amplitude ΔPSS (spherical average), FFR surrogate outputs and rupture-location index for each simulation case
Apply BC/inputs: inlet flow Dirichlet from data/input_parameter/inflow.dat, myocardium elastance BC data/input_parameter/elastance.dat, BC specification per data/cost_effective_FSI_BC/bc.md

Gaussian process regression surrogate modelling (ARD Matérn 5/2 + White noise kernel), input z-score normalization, output standardization, hyperparameter optimization with L-BFGS-B (20 restarts), 5-fold CV

Global sensitivity analysis using Saltelli sampling and Sobol index estimation (S1, ST) on the trained GPR surrogate (~15,000 base samples) with group- and parameter-level aggregation and convergence checks

Vulnerability index candidate generation and clinical sign-consistency screening: compute six candidate VIs (stress: peak PSS, ΔPSS × strength normalization scenarios E_fc^α for α variants) and score against seven established clinical high-risk plaque criteria using sign-consistency (1/0) and 95% BCa bootstrap CIs (1,000 resamples)
Inlet flow time series (coronary inflow waveform)
Cardiac elastance time series (myocardial BC)
Boundary-condition specification for cost-effective pulsatile FSI

Group-level Sobol results show the material-property group has the largest first-order contribution to VI variance for LAP·VI2 (material S1 ≈ 0.75) and similar dominance in CP results
Individual-parameter Sobol indicates E_fc and E_vessel are top contributors, followed by SBP and PP (e.g., E_fc S1 ≈ 0.55 for LAP·VI2)

Screening of six candidate VIs against seven clinical high-risk plaque criteria yielded two VIs (VI1=ΔPSS/E_fc^0.5, VI2=ΔPSS/E_fc^1.0) that satisfy all seven criteria with mean sign-consistency ≈1.00 (95% BCa CI 0.99–1.00)
Comparative analysis indicates ΔPSS (pulsatile amplitude) yields better alignment with clinical high-risk features and contributes more to selected VI performance than peak PSS
GPR surrogate cross-validation performance: 5-fold CV R² ≈0.93 (LAP) and ≈0.90 (CP), RMSE ≈0.12·σ(VI); posterior variance used as prediction uncertainty

Fatigue/failure mechanics principle: cyclic amplitude of stress (Δ-stress) is a key driver of fatigue damage accumulation and failure risk in materials, therefore ΔPSS better reflects fatigue-driven plaque rupture propensity than single-time peak stress

Normalization principle: risk metrics that compare load to local strength (stress/strength) provide a physically meaningful, dimensionless measure of failure likelihood across varying material properties

Sobol sensitivity theory: first-order (S1) indices quantify main effect contributions of input factors to output variance; group/parameter-level aggregation supports ranking of factor groups and parameters
Holzapfel 2004 (mechanical modeling limitations / stress-strength discussions)
Virmani 2000 (seven clinical high-risk plaque criteria)
Stone 2011 (PROSPECT, JACC; clinical plaque risk features)
Morris 2016 (PSS/FFR / rupture-location trend comparisons)
Sankaran 2017 (PSS/FFR comparisons)

VI 후보 6종(stress 2종 × strength 3시나리오)을 7개 임상 고위험 기준과의 부호일치로 평가한 결과, VI1=ΔPSS/E_fc^0.5와 VI2=ΔPSS/E_fc만 7기준을 모두 만족(부호일치 점수 평균 1.00, 95% BCa CI 0.99–1.00). 이 선별 결과(6개 중 2개만 전 기준 충족)가 "파열 취약성을 stress/strength 비율로 정의해야 한다"는 주장을 직접 지지하는 결과값이다. 근거: data/sobol/sobol_grp/ind_*_VI1/VI2.csv 및 후보 선별 표.

edges.rationale: Shows the stress metric choice (ΔPSS) yields better clinical consistency, justifying stress interpreted as pulsatile amplitude in the VI definition.
Explains why time-resolved FSI is necessary to compute ΔPSS and thus to implement the proposed stress/strength VI.
Empirical agreement with seven clinical criteria demonstrates that normalizing by E_fc yields clinically consistent VIs, motivating strength normalization.
Highlights that the specific normalization exponent α affects VI sensitivity to materials, supporting the claim that normalization choice matters.
Group-level Sobol S1 values quantify that material inputs explain the largest fraction of VI variance, supporting material dominance.
Individual-parameter Sobol rankings identify the specific dominant parameters (E_vessel, E_fc, SBP, PP), substantiating which material and hemodynamic variables drive VI.
Demonstrates that the selected VIs meet all clinical high-risk feature criteria, supporting their clinical plausibility.
Provides surrogate-evaluated diagnostic-performance evidence that the selected VI (especially VI2) can separate high-risk cases, supporting practical utility.
Group-level Sobol results (data/sobol/sobol_grp_LAP_VI2.csv) show material group S1 is the largest contributor (≈0.75) for LAP·VI2, supporting that materials dominate VI variability
Individual-parameter Sobol (data/sobol/sobol_ind_LAP_VI2.csv) ranks E_fc and E_vessel highest (E_fc S1 ≈0.55), with SBP and PP next, supporting parameter-level dominance
Group Sobol data for LAP·VI2 (data/sobol/sobol_grp_LAP_VI2.csv) show material group's first-order index ≈0.75, supporting the group-level dominance statement
Screening results from candidate VI sign-consistency scoring (method M4) identify VI1 and VI2 as the only candidates satisfying all seven clinical criteria, supporting selection of these VIs
Bootstrapped sign-consistency scoring reported mean=1.00 and 95% BCa CI 0.99–1.00 for VI1 and VI2, supporting the claim of full agreement with seven clinical criteria
Comparative postprocessing of FSI outputs indicates ΔPSS aligns better with clinical high-risk features and with selected VIs than peak PSS, supporting ΔPSS as a stronger predictor

Evidence that ΔPSS-based VIs (derived from pulsatile FSI outputs) outperform peak-stress metrics under clinical sign-consistency screening supports defining VI as stress/strength with stress=ΔPSS and implies necessity of pulsatile simulations
